AD.flag: France's blue and red on the outside, Spain's yellow and red inside — because Andorra is genuinely ruled by both.
AD.hook: Its two heads of state are the President of France and a Spanish bishop, neither of whom lives there. No airport, no army, and the average person lives longer than almost anyone on Earth.
AD.capital: Andorra la Vella — 'Andorra the town'. The highest capital in Europe at 1,023 m.

AE.flag: Red, green, white and black — all four pan-Arab colours, with the red standing vertically at the hoist.
AE.hook: Seven emirates that only became one country in 1971. Abu Dhabi holds almost all the oil; Dubai's ran low early, which is exactly why it built itself into a trading and tourist city instead.

AF.flag: Black, red and green with a white mosque emblem showing a mihrab and pulpit — black for a dark past, red for the blood of independence, green for hope.
AF.hook: Afghanistan has changed its flag more often than any country on Earth — more than twenty times in a century, which is its own kind of history lesson.

AG.flag: A rising gold sun on black, above blue and white, inside a red V for victory.
AG.hook: The country advertises 365 beaches — one for every day of the year — and its two islands together are smaller than most cities.

AI.flag: A British blue ensign with three orange dolphins leaping in a circle.
AI.hook: Anguilla rebelled in 1967 — to stay British. It broke away from a federation with St Kitts, and Britain eventually invaded with paratroopers and London policemen to end a revolution demanding its own rule.

AL.flag: A black double-headed eagle on blood red — the seal of Skanderbeg, the warlord who held the Ottomans off for 25 years. Two heads because Albania looks east and west at once.
AL.hook: A paranoid dictator built about 170,000 concrete bunkers here — one for every eleven people — against an invasion that never came. They are still in the fields, now used as cafés, storage and sheep shelters.

AM.flag: Red, blue and apricot. That bottom band really is named after the fruit — the apricot's scientific name is Prunus armeniaca.
AM.hook: The first country in the world to make Christianity its state religion, in 301 AD. Mount Ararat is its national symbol and sits just over the border in Turkey, visible from the capital but out of reach.

AO.flag: Red over black with a gold machete crossed with half a cogwheel, under a star — deliberately built on the pattern of the Soviet hammer and sickle.
AO.hook: The machete is for the farmers, the cogwheel for the factory workers. Angola also shelters the giant sable antelope, an animal thought extinct for decades until it turned up again in 2004.

AQ.flag: No official flag. The one usually shown is white with the continent's outline in the middle, proposed to stand for a place nobody owns.
AQ.hook: The coldest, driest, windiest and highest continent, governed by treaty instead of by a country. It has no permanent residents, no time zone of its own, and its dry valleys have not seen rain in millions of years.

AR.flag: Two light blue bands around white, with the Sun of May in the middle — and the sun has a human face, with 32 alternating straight and wavy rays.
AR.hook: Argentina holds the highest mountain outside Asia and the widest river on Earth: the Río de la Plata is 220 km across at its mouth.

AS.flag: A red-edged white triangle pointing at the hoist, with a bald eagle clutching a Samoan war club and fly-whisk.
AS.hook: Americans born here are US nationals but not automatically US citizens — the only place that is still true. It also sends more players per head to the NFL than anywhere else.

AT.flag: Red-white-red. Duke Leopold V came out of the Siege of Acre so drenched in blood that only the strip under his belt was still white.
AT.hook: Landlocked Austria kept a navy for centuries, and still has a saltwater admiral's legacy in Trieste. Also: no Austrian ever calls a pastry 'a Danish'.

AU.flag: A blue ensign with the Union Jack, the Southern Cross, and one large Commonwealth Star whose seven points are the six states plus the territories.
AU.hook: The only country that is also a whole continent. It has roughly twice as many kangaroos as people, and a fence longer than the Great Wall built to keep dingoes out of the sheep country.
AU.capital: Canberra was built from nothing as a compromise because Sydney and Melbourne could not agree which of them should be the capital.

AW.flag: Light blue for the sea with two yellow stripes and a red four-pointed star edged in white.
AW.hook: A Dutch Caribbean island outside the hurricane belt, which is why it is dry, cactus-covered and full of tourists. Its people speak Papiamento, a creole blending Portuguese, Spanish, Dutch and African languages.

AX.flag: The Swedish flag's blue and gold with a red Nordic cross laid inside — Sweden's colours, Finland's sovereignty.
AX.hook: A Swedish-speaking, demilitarised archipelago of some 6,700 islands that belongs to Finland. It has had its own parliament since 1920 and its own postage stamps.

AZ.flag: Blue for Turkic heritage, red for progress, green for Islam, with a white crescent and an eight-pointed star for eight Turkic peoples.
AZ.hook: The Land of Fire: natural gas seeps have burned on its hillsides for thousands of years without ever going out. It also has about half the world's mud volcanoes.

BA.flag: A yellow triangle whose three points are the three peoples, sitting roughly where the country sits, with Europe's stars running off the edge in both directions.
BA.hook: The design was imposed from outside on purpose: every colour the locals proposed belonged to one ethnic group, so the UN picked blue and yellow because they belonged to nobody.

BB.flag: Blue, gold, blue with a black trident head — and look closely: the shaft is broken off. That break is independence from Britain.
BB.hook: The broken trident is the whole message. Barbados is also made of coral rather than volcanic rock, which is why it sits flat while its neighbours are mountainous.

BD.flag: A red sun on bottle green — and the disc is deliberately off-centre, nudged toward the mast so it looks centred when the flag is flying.
BD.hook: It sits on the largest river delta on Earth, and its Sundarbans mangroves hold tigers that routinely swim between islands.

BE.flag: Black, yellow, red — lifted from the gold lion with red claws on a black shield of Brabant. It is the rare tricolour that is nearly square.
BE.hook: Belgium once went 589 days without a government and barely noticed. It also has the world's densest railway network and invented the saxophone.

BF.flag: Red over green with a gold star, the star being the guiding light of the revolution.
BF.hook: The name was invented in 1984 and stitched together from two different local languages to mean 'land of upright people'. Its citizens are Burkinabè, a word borrowed from a third.

BG.flag: Russia's white-blue-red with the blue swapped for green — white for peace, green for the farmland, red for the blood it cost.
BG.hook: Bulgarians nod their head for no and shake it for yes. They also grow most of the world's rose oil, and the Cyrillic alphabet was invented here, not in Russia.

BH.flag: White and red split by a five-point zigzag — one point for each pillar of Islam. Count the points and you can tell it from Qatar.
BH.hook: An island nation that was the pearl-diving capital of the world until Japan invented cultured pearls and the trade collapsed almost overnight.

BI.flag: A white saltire dividing red and green, with three red stars in the middle for unity, work and progress — and for the three peoples of the country.
BI.hook: Burundi's royal drummers are UNESCO-listed: the drums were once sacred objects played only for the king, and are struck while dancing with them balanced on the head.
BI.capital: Gitega took over as political capital from Bujumbura in 2019.

BJ.flag: A green vertical band with yellow over red — the pan-African colours in a layout nobody else uses.
BJ.hook: This was the Kingdom of Dahomey, which fielded an all-female army so effective that Europeans called them the Dahomey Amazons. Vodun — voodoo — is a recognised national religion here, where it began.
BJ.capital: Porto-Novo is the official capital, but the government actually sits in Cotonou.

BL.flag: Flies the French tricolour, with a local white flag bearing three fleurs-de-lis, a Maltese cross and three crowns.
BL.hook: Sweden owned this Caribbean island for almost a century and sold it back to France in 1878, which is why the capital is called Gustavia. Its airport requires a special pilot licence — planes drop over a hill straight onto the runway.

BM.flag: A British red ensign — unusual, as most territories use blue — with a coat of arms showing a lion holding a shield with a shipwreck.
BM.hook: That shipwreck is the Sea Venture, which ran aground in 1609 and accidentally founded the colony. The survivors' story is thought to have given Shakespeare The Tempest. Bermuda is in the Atlantic off North Carolina, nowhere near the Caribbean.

BN.flag: Royal yellow slashed with black and white, under a red emblem of a parasol, a crescent and two upheld hands.
BN.hook: The Sultan's palace has 1,788 rooms and 257 bathrooms. There is no income tax, petrol costs less than water, and the whole country sits on the island of Borneo with Malaysia and Indonesia.

BO.flag: Red, yellow and green — and Bolivia has a second official flag flown beside it, the Wiphala, a seven-colour rainbow checkerboard of the Andean peoples.
BO.hook: The Salar de Uyuni is the largest salt flat on Earth and so perfectly level that satellites use it to calibrate their altimeters. After rain it becomes the world's biggest mirror.
BO.capital: Sucre is the constitutional capital; La Paz holds the government and sits at 3,600 m, the highest seat of government anywhere.

BQ.flag: No single flag — Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba each fly their own; the Dutch tricolour covers them all.
BQ.hook: Three Caribbean islands that are literally municipalities of the Netherlands, so the highest point in the Kingdom of the Netherlands is a Caribbean volcano on Saba, not anything in Europe.

BR.flag: A blue globe on a yellow diamond on green, with 27 stars and 'Ordem e Progresso' across it.
BR.hook: Those stars are not decoration: they are the actual sky over Rio de Janeiro on the morning of 15 November 1889, the day the republic was declared — drawn as if viewed from outside the celestial sphere, so the constellations are mirrored.

BS.flag: Aquamarine and gold stripes with a black triangle driving in from the hoist — sea, sand, and the people's determination.
BS.hook: About 700 islands, only 30 of them lived on. Dean's Blue Hole plunges 202 m straight down, and one cay is populated entirely by pigs that swim out to meet boats.

BT.flag: A white thunder dragon clutching jewels, split diagonally between the king's yellow and Buddhism's orange. The dragon is Druk, and his growl is thunder.
BT.hook: Bhutan measures Gross National Happiness instead of GDP, is the only carbon-negative country in the world, and did not allow television until 1999.

BV.hook: The most remote island on Earth: an uninhabited volcanic rock under a glacier, 1,600 km from Antarctica and 2,600 km from South Africa. In 1964 an abandoned lifeboat was found there and nobody has ever explained it.

BW.flag: Pale blue for rain, cut by a black stripe between two white ones — for the people living together, and for the zebra.
BW.hook: Water matters so much that the currency is called the pula, which means 'rain', and is also how you say hello and give thanks. A third of Africa's elephants live here.

BY.flag: Red and green, with a white-and-red band of embroidery down the hoist — a rushnyk, the woven ritual towel of Belarusian households. It is the only national flag carrying a textile pattern.
BY.hook: A third of the country is forest and swamp, including Europe's last primeval woodland, where wild bison were brought back from twelve surviving animals.

BZ.flag: Blue with red bands and a large coat of arms showing two woodcutters — one Black, one mestizo — flanking a mahogany tree.
BZ.hook: The only national flag with human beings as its main subject. Belize is also the only Central American country whose official language is English, and its Great Blue Hole is a collapsed cave visible from space.

CA.flag: A red maple leaf between two red bars. The leaf has eleven points for no symbolic reason at all — earlier designs blurred into a red smudge in wind tunnel tests, and eleven points stayed legible.
CA.hook: Canada has more lake surface than the rest of the world put together, and a longer coastline than any other country by a huge margin.

CC.flag: Green with a palm tree, a crescent and the Southern Cross.
CC.hook: Two coral atolls in the Indian Ocean run for over a century as a private fiefdom by one Scottish family, the Clunies-Ross, until Australia bought them out in 1978.

CD.flag: Sky blue cut by a red diagonal edged in yellow, with a gold star in the upper corner.
CD.hook: Roughly the size of Western Europe. The Congo is the deepest river on Earth at over 220 m, deep enough that fish at the bottom evolved blind and separately from those above.
CD.capital: Kinshasa faces Brazzaville across the river — the two closest capitals of different countries anywhere except Rome and the Vatican.

CF.flag: Four horizontal bands — blue, white, green, yellow — with a single red stripe running vertically straight through them, and a gold star in the corner.
CF.hook: The red bar is the whole idea: the blue and white of Europe and the green and yellow of Africa, joined by the blood that both share.

CG.flag: A yellow diagonal separating green from red — one of very few flags divided corner to corner.
CG.hook: This is the smaller Congo, the one whose capital is Brazzaville. Its neighbour across the river is DR Congo, whose capital is Kinshasa. The two stare at each other over the water.

CH.flag: Square — one of only two square national flags, with the Vatican. A white cross on red, and if you reverse the colours you get the Red Cross, named for the Swiss who founded it.
CH.hook: Switzerland has enough nuclear shelter space for its entire population, and its bridges and tunnels are wired with demolition charges in case of invasion.

CI.flag: Orange, white and green — the Irish flag with the colours reversed, which the two countries have had to explain to each other more than once.
CI.hook: The world's largest cocoa producer by a wide margin, and home to the largest church building on Earth, a basilica in the middle of a town of 200,000.
CI.capital: Yamoussoukro is the official capital; Abidjan is where almost everything actually happens.

CK.flag: A blue ensign with the Union Jack and fifteen white stars in a ring — one for each inhabited island.
CK.hook: Self-governing in free association with New Zealand. There are roughly 15,000 Cook Islanders at home and perhaps five times that many living in New Zealand.

CL.flag: White over red with a blue square and a single white star — 'la estrella solitaria', the lone star, for a unitary state.
CL.hook: Chile is 4,300 km long and averages under 180 km wide. Parts of the Atacama have weather stations that have never once recorded rainfall.

CM.flag: Green, red and yellow vertical with a gold star centred on the red.
CM.hook: Called 'Africa in miniature' because it packs desert, rainforest, savanna, mountains and coast into one country. Mount Cameroon is an active volcano that rises straight out of the Atlantic.

CN.flag: One big gold star for the Communist Party, four small ones for the classes of society — and each small star is rotated so its point aims at the big one.
CN.hook: China spans five geographic time zones but legally runs on one, so the sun can rise at 10 am in the west. Every giant panda in every zoo on Earth is rented from China.

CO.flag: Yellow taking up the whole top half, then blue and red — the yellow is doubled because it stands for the country's gold and wealth.
CO.hook: The only South American country with coasts on both the Caribbean and the Pacific, and it records more bird species than any other nation on Earth.

CR.flag: Blue, white and a doubled red band through the middle — the red was added in 1848 in sympathy with the French Revolution.
CR.hook: Costa Rica abolished its army in 1948 and put the budget into schools and hospitals. It holds about 5% of all known species on 0.03% of the world's land.

CU.flag: Five stripes with a red triangle and a white star. The triangle and its colours come from freemasonry — liberty, equality, fraternity.
CU.hook: Cuba's flag and Puerto Rico's are exactly the same design with the red and blue swapped. The two were drafted by allied independence movements in the same period.

CV.flag: Deep blue with a white and red band, and a ring of ten gold stars.
CV.hook: Ten stars for ten islands, arranged in a circle because that is roughly how the archipelago sits in the ocean. Nobody lived here at all before the Portuguese arrived in 1456.

CW.flag: Blue with a yellow stripe and two white stars — for Curaçao and Klein Curaçao.
CW.hook: The blue liqueur is from here, made from the peel of a bitter orange that Spanish settlers planted and the dry climate ruined into something new. Willemstad's Dutch gabled houses are painted in sweets colours.

CX.flag: Split blue and green diagonally, with the Southern Cross, a golden bosun bird and a map of the island.
CX.hook: Every year around 50 million red crabs walk from the forest to the sea to spawn, and the island closes roads and builds bridges for them. It belongs to Australia but sits closer to Java.

CY.flag: One of only two flags that draw their own country's outline. The island is copper-orange because Cyprus *is* copper — the metal is named after the island.
CY.hook: The last divided capital in Europe runs through the middle of it, with a UN buffer zone where a 1974 airport still sits with a rotting jet on the apron.

CZ.flag: White over red, with a blue wedge driven in from the hoist — the blue was added purely so nobody would mistake it for Poland.
CZ.hook: Czechs drink more beer per person than anyone alive, and gave the world the word 'robot', from a 1920 play about artificial workers.
CZ.capital: Prague sits on the Vltava, and its castle is the largest ancient castle complex in the world.

DE.flag: Black, red, gold — the uniform of the Lützow Free Corps who fought Napoleon: black coats, red facings, brass buttons.
DE.hook: German has an official word for the guilt of eating too much, and the Autobahn still has stretches with no speed limit at all.

DJ.flag: Light blue for sea and sky, green for earth, and a white triangle with a red star for unity and independence.
DJ.hook: Lake Assal is the lowest point in Africa and the saltiest body of water outside Antarctica. Djibouti is also the only place where American, Chinese, French, Japanese and Italian military bases sit within a few kilometres of each other.

DK.flag: The Dannebrog — the oldest national flag still in use. Legend says it fell out of the sky mid-battle in Estonia in 1219. The cross sits off-centre because that is where it lands when a flag hangs.
DK.hook: Every other Nordic flag is a copy of this one. Denmark is also flatter than almost anywhere — its highest natural point is a 171 m hill people drive to on purpose.

DM.flag: Green with a yellow, black and white cross and a red disc holding a sisserou parrot ringed by ten stars.
DM.hook: That parrot makes this the only national flag in the world containing purple. The bird lives nowhere else, and there are only a few hundred left.

DO.flag: Blue and red quartered by a white cross, with a coat of arms in the centre — and in the arms, an open Bible.
DO.hook: The only national flag on Earth with a Bible on it, turned to the Gospel of John: 'and the truth shall make you free'. The island it shares with Haiti holds the Caribbean's highest and lowest points.

DZ.flag: Green and white split down the middle with a red crescent and star sitting across the join. The crescent's horns are unusually long — Algerians say long horns bring happiness.
DZ.hook: The largest country in Africa, and about four-fifths of it is Sahara. It only became the biggest when Sudan split in two in 2011.

EC.flag: Yellow, blue and red with a condor spreading its wings over a shield showing Chimborazo and a steamship.
EC.hook: Ecuador is named after the equator. Because the planet bulges at the middle, the summit of Chimborazo is the point on Earth's surface furthest from its centre — further out than Everest.

EE.flag: Blue, black, white: the sky and lakes, the soil and the peasant's coat, and the snow and birch bark.
EE.hook: Estonia files taxes online in about three minutes, invented Skype, and sells digital residency to foreigners who have never set foot there.

EG.flag: Red, white and black with the gold Eagle of Saladin in the centre.
EG.hook: Egypt is essentially one river with a country attached: about 95% of Egyptians live on the 5% of land within reach of the Nile.

EH.flag: Black, white and green with a red triangle, crescent and star — the flag of the Sahrawi republic.
EH.hook: Africa's last unresolved colonial question. Morocco controls most of it behind a 2,700 km sand wall — one of the longest barriers on Earth — while a government-in-exile runs refugee camps in Algeria.

ER.flag: A red triangle carrying a gold olive wreath, wedged between green and blue.
ER.hook: Asmara is a complete Italian Art Deco city dropped in the Horn of Africa and left almost untouched — futurist petrol stations, cinemas and all — and it is UNESCO-listed for exactly that.

ES.flag: Red-yellow-red, picked by Charles III in 1785 for a practical reason — he wanted Spanish ships identifiable from a long way off at sea, and no other navy used that combination.
ES.hook: The Spanish national anthem has no words; people hum it. Spain also has the world's oldest restaurant still operating, open since 1725.

ET.flag: Green, yellow and red with a blue disc and a gold star radiating light.
ET.hook: This is where the pan-African colours come from. Ethiopia was never colonised, so newly independent African states copied its flag as a badge of that. It also keeps its own calendar of thirteen months, running seven to eight years behind the rest of the world.

FI.flag: A blue Nordic cross on white — the lakes and the snow, nothing more.
FI.hook: 188,000 lakes and more saunas than cars. Finland also runs a world championship in carrying your wife, and the prize is her weight in beer.

FJ.flag: Pale sky blue for the Pacific, with the Union Jack and a shield of sugar cane, a coconut palm, bananas and a dove.
FJ.hook: Fiji voted to remove the Union Jack in 2015 and then quietly dropped the idea. Its 333 islands sit right on the 180th meridian, so the date line had to be bent around them.

FK.flag: A blue ensign with a coat of arms: a ram above the ship Desire, which sighted the islands in 1592.
FK.hook: Around 3,500 people and roughly half a million sheep. Argentina and Britain fought a 74-day war over them in 1982.

FM.flag: UN light blue with four white stars in a diamond — one for each of the four states.
FM.hook: Micronesia's 607 islands are spread over an area of ocean bigger than the continental United States. On Pohnpei sits Nan Madol, a city of nearly a hundred artificial islands built from stacked basalt logs.

FO.flag: The Merkið: a red Nordic cross edged in blue on white — the white being the sea foam and the sky.
FO.hook: Eighteen North Atlantic islands with more sheep than people, where grass roofs are still standard and a village church may be reached by tunnel. Faroese sheepdogs wear cameras for the islands' own answer to Street View.

FR.flag: Blue and red are the colours of Paris; white was the king's. The Revolution put the monarch between the mob and left him there.
FR.hook: France is the most-visited country on Earth, and thanks to Guiana, Réunion and the Pacific it has a land border with Brazil and territory in every ocean.
FR.capital: Paris — every road distance in France is measured from a brass star outside Notre-Dame.

GA.flag: Green, yellow and blue: the forest on top, the equator as a gold line through the middle, the sea below.
GA.hook: Almost 90% forest, and the president set aside 11% of the country as national park in one go after seeing footage of hippos surfing in the Atlantic.

GB.flag: Three crosses stacked: England's red cross of St George, Scotland's white saltire of St Andrew, and Ireland's red saltire of St Patrick. The saltires are deliberately offset, so the flag has a right way up and can be flown upside down by mistake.
GB.hook: Wales is nowhere on it. It had already been absorbed into England when the flag was designed, so the dragon never got a look in.

GD.flag: A red border with six gold stars, a seventh in a central disc, and — on the hoist triangle — a nutmeg.
GD.hook: The only national flag with a nutmeg on it. Grenada has supplied a large share of the world's nutmeg for two centuries, which is why it is called the Isle of Spice.

GE.flag: The five-cross flag: one big red St George's cross with four small ones in the corners, a medieval banner brought back in 2004.
GE.hook: Wine was invented here. Georgians have been fermenting grapes in buried clay qvevri for 8,000 years, and the alphabet they write it down in looks like no other script in the world.

GF.flag: Officially flies the French tricolour; an unofficial green and yellow flag with a red star is widely used.
GF.hook: Part of France, in the European Union, using the euro — on the coast of South America. Europe launches its rockets from here because sites near the equator get a free speed boost from the Earth's spin.

GG.flag: England's red St George's cross with a gold Norman cross laid inside it, added in 1985 to tell Guernsey from England.
GG.hook: A Crown Dependency that is not in the UK and never joined the EU. It still uses its own pound, and its parliament has met since the 13th century.

GH.flag: Red, gold and green with a black five-pointed star — the Black Star, taken from Marcus Garvey's Black Star shipping line.
GH.hook: The first sub-Saharan colony to win independence, in 1957. Half of Africa borrowed its colours afterwards, and its football team is still called the Black Stars.

GI.flag: White and red with a three-towered red castle and a gold key hanging from it — the key to the Mediterranean.
GI.hook: A 6.7 km² limestone headland at the mouth of the Mediterranean, holding Europe's only wild monkeys. Legend says if the macaques leave, the British will too, so Churchill ordered more shipped in during the war.

GL.flag: The Erfalasorput: a white and red disc on a white and red field, where the top half of the circle is the sun and the bottom half the sea ice.
GL.hook: The world's largest island, three-quarters covered by an ice sheet up to 3 km thick. Because Mercator maps stretch the poles, it looks the size of Africa when it is fourteen times smaller.

GM.flag: Red, blue and green separated by thin white lines — the sun above, the river between, the land below. It is a cross-section of the country.
GM.hook: The Gambia is the smallest country on mainland Africa: a thin ribbon following the river inland, surrounded on three sides by Senegal and never more than about 50 km wide.

GN.flag: Red, yellow and green in vertical bands — the pan-African colours stood upright, French tricolour style.
GN.hook: Guinea sits on roughly a quarter of the world's known bauxite, the ore behind almost all aluminium. The Niger, Senegal and Gambia rivers all rise in its highlands.

GP.flag: Flies the French tricolour; a local flag shows a sun and sugar cane on black with a yellow stripe.
GP.hook: A butterfly-shaped pair of islands in the Caribbean that is fully part of France and the EU. One wing is a flat limestone plateau, the other a volcanic rainforest with an active volcano.

GQ.flag: Green, white and red with a blue triangle, and a coat of arms showing a silk-cotton tree — the 'God tree' — under six stars for the mainland and five islands.
GQ.hook: The only African country where Spanish is official. Its capital is not on the mainland at all but on a volcanic island 40 km offshore.

GR.flag: Nine blue and white stripes, said to be the nine syllables of 'Eleftheria i Thanatos' — freedom or death. The cross is for the Orthodox church.
GR.hook: Greece has around 6,000 islands and inhabits about 227 of them. No point in the country is more than 137 km from the sea.

GS.flag: A blue ensign with a shield holding a fur seal, a macaroni penguin and a reindeer.
GS.hook: No permanent population, but several million seals and penguins. Shackleton is buried here, having crossed the island's unmapped mountains in 36 hours to fetch rescue for his stranded crew.

GT.flag: Sky blue and white vertical bands with a coat of arms: a resplendent quetzal above a scroll dated 1821, crossed rifles and swords.
GT.hook: The quetzal is the national bird, the national currency, and reputedly dies in captivity — which is why it stands for liberty. Tikal's temples rise straight out of the rainforest canopy.

GU.flag: Dark blue with a red border and an almond-shaped seal showing a proa sailing past a coconut palm and a cliff.
GU.hook: About a third of the island is a US military base, and locals call it 'where America's day begins' because of the date line. Guam also lost its native bird species to brown tree snakes that arrived as cargo stowaways.

GW.flag: A red vertical band with a black star, beside yellow over green.
GW.hook: Cashews make up most of what the country sells abroad. Its Bijagós archipelago is one of the few places where saltwater hippos swim between islands in the Atlantic.

GY.flag: The Golden Arrowhead: a gold arrow on green, with a red triangle, fimbriated in black and white.
GY.hook: The only South American country whose official language is English — it looks to the Caribbean, not to Latin America. Kaieteur Falls drops 226 m in a single uninterrupted sheet.

HK.flag: Red with a white five-petalled bauhinia flower, each petal carrying a small red star.
HK.hook: More skyscrapers than any other city on Earth, and about three-quarters of the territory is undeveloped country park and mountain. The flower on the flag is a sterile hybrid found in 1880 — every bauhinia blakeana alive is a cutting of that one tree.

HM.hook: An uninhabited Australian territory in the sub-Antarctic holding Big Ben, an active volcano and Australia's highest mountain — higher than anything on the mainland. Almost nobody has ever landed there.

HN.flag: Blue, white, blue with five blue stars arranged in an X across the white band.
HN.hook: The five stars are the five states of the old Federal Republic of Central America, kept on the flag as a standing wish that it will one day reassemble. The term 'banana republic' was coined about Honduras.

HR.flag: The šahovnica — a 25-square red and white chessboard — sitting on a red-white-blue field.
HR.hook: The necktie is Croatian. 'Cravat' is just 'Croat': French officers copied the knotted scarves of Croatian mercenaries in the 1600s and never took them off.

HT.flag: Blue over red. When Haitian revolutionaries made it, they took the French tricolour and tore the white out of the middle, then sewed the remaining halves together.
HT.hook: That gesture is the flag. Haiti is the only nation founded by a successful slave revolt, and the first Black republic in the world.

HU.flag: Red for strength, white for faith, green for hope.
HU.hook: Hungarian is related to nothing around it — its closest relatives are spoken in Finland and Siberia. The Rubik's Cube, the biro and the Ford Model T's engineer are all Hungarian.

ID.flag: Red over white, and identical to Monaco's except that Indonesia's is longer. Red for the body, white for the soul.
ID.hook: More than 17,000 islands and over 700 living languages. It is currently building a brand new capital in the jungle of Borneo because Jakarta is sinking by up to 25 cm a year.
ID.capital: Jakarta is the capital today, but the government is moving to Nusantara — a city being built from scratch.

IE.flag: Green for the Catholic Gaelic tradition, orange for the Protestant followers of William of Orange, and white for a truce between them. The flag is a peace proposal.
IE.hook: Ireland has no snakes, no moles and no native rats. Halloween started here as Samhain, and the word 'boycott' is named after an unpopular Irish land agent.

IL.flag: A blue Star of David between two blue bands on white — the bands come from the tallit, the striped prayer shawl.
IL.hook: The Dead Sea shore is the lowest dry land on the planet, 430 m below sea level, and so salty that floating is involuntary.

IM.flag: Red with the triskelion: three armoured legs joined at the hip, running clockwise.
IM.hook: Its parliament, Tynwald, claims to be the oldest continuously running one in the world, at over a thousand years. The island also has tailless Manx cats and a motorcycle race on public roads that has killed over 260 riders.

IN.flag: Saffron, white and green around the Ashoka Chakra — a 24-spoke wheel taken from a 3rd-century BC lion capital. It replaced Gandhi's spinning wheel at the last minute.
IN.hook: India has no national language. It has 22 official ones, and every banknote carries the amount written in seventeen different scripts.
IN.capital: New Delhi was built next to Old Delhi, not on top of it — so the country's capital and its 17th-century predecessor sit side by side.

IO.flag: A blue ensign with wavy blue and white lines, a palm tree and a crown.
IO.hook: Britain removed the entire population in the 1960s and 70s so the United States could build an airbase on Diego Garcia. The courts have argued about it ever since, and in 2024 Britain agreed to hand the islands to Mauritius.

IQ.flag: Red, white and black with 'Allahu Akbar' written across the middle in green Kufic script.
IQ.hook: This is Mesopotamia: writing, the wheel, the 60-minute hour and the first cities all start here. The marshes of the south are thought by some to be the original Garden of Eden.

IR.flag: Green, white and red with an emblem shaped like a tulip that also spells 'Allah'. Along the inner edges of the stripes, 'Allahu Akbar' is written 22 times in angular Kufic script.
IR.hook: Those 22 repetitions mark 22 Bahman, the date of the 1979 revolution. Iran also runs on a solar calendar where new year falls on the spring equinox, and the country is mostly high desert plateau, not sand dunes.

IS.flag: A Nordic cross made of the island's own geology: blue ocean, white ice, red volcanic fire.
IS.hook: No mosquitoes, no surnames — Icelanders are named after their father, so the phone book is alphabetised by first name. New volcanic islands occasionally just appear.

IT.flag: Modelled on the French tricolour, but the green came from the uniforms of the Milanese civic guard.
IT.hook: Italy has more UNESCO World Heritage sites than any country, and completely surrounds two other countries — San Marino and the Vatican.

JE.flag: A red saltire on white with the Plantagenet crown and Jersey's three leopards.
JE.hook: Closer to France than to England, with its own language descended from Norman French. Jersey cows all trace back to this island, where importing any other breed was banned for two centuries.

JM.flag: A gold saltire splitting the field into green and black triangles.
JM.hook: The only national flag on Earth that contains none of red, white or blue. Jamaica also produced both reggae and the world's fastest humans from a population of under three million.

JO.flag: Black, white and green with a red triangle and a seven-pointed star — seven for the verses of the opening chapter of the Quran.
JO.hook: Add the star and you have Jordan; take it away and you have Palestine. Jordan also hides Petra, a city carved directly into a rose-red canyon wall.

JP.flag: The Hinomaru: a red sun disc on white. That is the whole flag, and it has been the whole flag for centuries.
JP.hook: Japan is made of about 14,000 islands and has more than four million vending machines. Its imperial line is the oldest continuous hereditary monarchy in the world.

KE.flag: Black, red and green with white edges, and a red Maasai shield with two crossed spears in the centre.
KE.hook: The shield and spears mean the defence of freedom. The Great Rift Valley runs through the country, and the highlands around it have produced more world-record distance runners than anywhere else.

KG.flag: A red field with a gold sun of 40 rays for the 40 tribes — and inside the sun, the crossed roof-crown of a yurt seen from directly below.
KG.hook: You are looking up through the smoke hole of a nomad's tent. The country is 90% mountains, and its great lake never freezes despite sitting at 1,600 m.

KH.flag: The only national flag on Earth with a building on it: the three towers of Angkor Wat, in white on red.
KH.hook: Angkor was the largest pre-industrial city in the world, home to perhaps a million people when London had 30,000.

KI.flag: A golden frigatebird flying over a rising sun and three white waves. The sun has seventeen rays for the sixteen Gilbert Islands plus Banaba.
KI.hook: Kiribati straddles both the equator and the date line, which puts it in all four hemispheres at once. In 1995 it shoved the date line east around its own territory so the whole country shared one day — which also made it the first place on Earth to reach the year 2000.

KM.flag: Four stripes and four stars for four islands, behind a green triangle with a crescent.
KM.hook: One of those four islands is Mayotte, which voted to remain French — so Comoros permanently flies a flag claiming an island it has never governed. It also grows most of the world's ylang-ylang, the base note in a great deal of perfume.

KN.flag: A black diagonal band edged in yellow carrying two white stars, between green and red.
KN.hook: The smallest sovereign state in the Americas by both area and population. Its two islands are separated by a 3 km channel called The Narrows.

KP.flag: Blue, red and blue with white fimbriations and a red star inside a white disc, set toward the hoist.
KP.hook: North Korea keeps its own calendar, counting years from Kim Il-sung's birth in 1912, and its own time zone, which it moved by 30 minutes and then moved back.

KR.flag: The red and blue taegeuk of balance, ringed by four black trigrams from the I Ching: heaven, earth, fire and water.
KR.hook: The only national flag drawing on the I Ching. About one in five South Koreans is surnamed Kim, and the country went from poorer than Ghana to a top-15 economy inside one lifetime.

KW.flag: Green, white and red stripes with a black shape at the hoist — and look closely, it is a trapezoid, not a triangle.
KW.hook: When retreating troops set the oil wells alight in 1991, more than 600 fires burned for nine months and turned day into night.

KY.flag: A blue ensign with a shield of three stars for the three islands, a turtle, a pineapple and a lion.
KY.hook: More registered companies than people, by a wide margin. The turtle is there because Columbus originally called the islands Las Tortugas for the sea turtles crowding the water.

KZ.flag: A sky-blue field with a gold sun of 32 rays above a steppe eagle, and a band of national ornament running down the hoist.
KZ.hook: The largest landlocked country in the world — bigger than all of Western Europe. Every Russian cosmonaut still launches from Baikonur, on Kazakh soil.
KZ.capital: Astana simply means 'capital'. It was renamed Nur-Sultan in 2019 and changed back in 2022.

LA.flag: Red, blue and red with a white disc — the full moon over the Mekong river.
LA.hook: Laos is the most heavily bombed country per person in history: more ordnance fell here than on all of Europe in WWII, and teams are still clearing it.

LB.flag: Red, white, red with a green cedar of Lebanon in the middle, its trunk and leaves both green.
LB.hook: That tree is in the Bible — cedar from these mountains built Solomon's temple and Egyptian ships. Only a few small groves are left.

LC.flag: A black arrowhead edged in white rising out of a gold triangle, on blue — the Pitons standing out of the sea.
LC.hook: Saint Lucia has produced two Nobel laureates from a population of under 200,000, which is more per person than any other country. It also changed hands between Britain and France fourteen times.

LI.flag: Blue over red with a gold crown — and the crown is there because of an embarrassment. At the 1936 Olympics Liechtenstein discovered its flag was identical to Haiti's, and added the crown the next year.
LI.hook: You can rent the entire country for the night. It has no airport, makes more false teeth than anywhere, and its army was disbanded in 1868 after returning from war with one more man than it left with.

LK.flag: A gold lion holding a sword on maroon, with a bo leaf in each corner, and two stripes at the hoist for the Tamil and Muslim communities.
LK.hook: The only flag with a lion wielding a weapon. Sri Lanka also elected the world's first female prime minister, in 1960.
LK.capital: Colombo is the commercial capital, but parliament sits in Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte next door.

LR.flag: Eleven stripes and a single white star on blue — a deliberate copy of the American flag, because Liberia was founded by freed slaves from the United States.
LR.hook: Eleven stripes for the eleven signatories of its declaration of independence. Because its ship registry is so cheap and permissive, a large share of the world's merchant fleet flies this flag without ever visiting.

LS.flag: Blue, white and green with a black mokorotlo — the conical Basotho straw hat — in the middle.
LS.hook: The only country in the world entirely above 1,000 m, and one of only three completely surrounded by a single other country. It snows here, in southern Africa.

LT.flag: Yellow for the sun and the wheat, green for the forests, red for the blood spilled defending both.
LT.hook: The last pagan state in Europe, holding out until 1387. It also has a hill covered with more than 100,000 crosses that the Soviets bulldozed three times and locals rebuilt every time.

LU.flag: Red, white and light blue — so close to the Dutch flag that the country adopted a second, striped lion banner to tell them apart.
LU.hook: The only remaining sovereign grand duchy on Earth, with the highest GDP per person and a public transport network that is entirely free.

LV.flag: Carmine — a deep brownish red — with a narrow white stripe. A wounded chief was wrapped in a white sheet; the edges soaked through, the middle where he lay stayed clean.
LV.hook: Riga has more art nouveau buildings than any city in the world, and Latvia is over half forest and getting greener every year.

LY.flag: Red, black and green with a white crescent and star, the black band twice as tall as the others.
LY.hook: From 1977 to 2011 Libya flew a plain green rectangle with nothing on it — the only entirely blank single-colour national flag in history.

MA.flag: Red with a green interlaced pentagram — the Seal of Solomon, drawn as a single unbroken line.
MA.hook: Morocco was the first country to recognise the United States, in 1777, and the two have the longest unbroken treaty in American history. Fez holds the oldest continuously operating university in the world, founded in 859 by a woman.

MC.flag: Red over white, the Grimaldi family colours — and identical to Indonesia's except that Monaco's is squatter.
MC.hook: Smaller than New York's Central Park, with more millionaires per head than anywhere. Its royal family has ruled for over 700 years, and the Grand Prix runs through ordinary streets that reopen on Monday.

MD.flag: Blue, yellow, red with an aurochs head between a star, a rose and a crescent. Look at the back and the emblem is missing — one of a handful of flags that differ on each side.
MD.hook: Beneath Moldova lie 200 km of tunnels holding the largest wine collection on Earth. Staff get around the cellar by car.

ME.flag: Deep red with a gold border and a crowned double-headed eagle — closer to a royal standard than a flag.
ME.hook: The name means 'black mountain'. It is one of the newest countries in Europe, and the only one that declares itself an 'ecological state' in its constitution.

MF.flag: Flies the French tricolour; a local flag shows the island's arms on white.
MF.hook: The island is split between France and the Netherlands, and the 1648 border has held ever since with no fence and no checkpoint — the smallest land mass in the world divided between two nations.

MG.flag: A white vertical band beside red over green — white and red from the old Merina kingdom, green for the coastal peoples.
MG.hook: Madagascar broke off from Africa around 160 million years ago, and about 90% of its wildlife exists nowhere else. Every wild lemur on Earth is here.

MH.flag: Blue with an orange and a white band widening as they rise from the hoist, under a 24-pointed white star.
MH.hook: The rising bands are the islands climbing out of the equator; the star's 24 points are the districts. The United States tested 67 nuclear weapons here, and the bikini swimsuit is named after the atoll they vaporised.
MH.capital: Majuro is on an atoll so narrow that in places you can see ocean on both sides from the middle of the road.

MK.flag: A gold sun with eight rays widening to the edges — 'the new sun of liberty'. It replaced an older sun design after Greece objected to it.
MK.hook: Landlocked, but Lake Ohrid on its border is three million years old, one of the oldest lakes on the planet. Mother Teresa was born in Skopje.

ML.flag: Green, yellow and red vertical bands, with no emblem — an Islamic objection to depicting the human figure removed the original stick figure in 1961.
ML.hook: Timbuktu was a university town when Oxford was new, and families there still hide hundreds of thousands of medieval manuscripts. Mali's 14th-century ruler Mansa Musa may have been the richest individual who ever lived.

MM.flag: Yellow, green and red with one large white star — solidarity, peace, courage.
MM.hook: Myanmar switched from driving on the left to the right in 1970, reportedly on an astrologer's advice, but kept importing right-hand-drive cars. Bus doors now open into the traffic.
MM.capital: Naypyidaw was built in secret and unveiled in 2005. It has a twenty-lane highway that is almost always empty.

MN.flag: The gold Soyombo column: fire above sun and moon, two downward arrowheads aimed at enemies, and two fish — which never close their eyes, so they stand for vigilance.
MN.hook: The least densely populated sovereign country in the world, with more horses than people and a capital that is the coldest on Earth.

MO.flag: Green with a white lotus above a stylised bridge and water, under five gold stars.
MO.hook: The most densely populated place on Earth, and its casinos take in several times the revenue of Las Vegas. Portuguese is still an official language, though almost nobody speaks it.

MP.flag: Blue with a white star over a grey latte stone — a pillar the ancient Chamorro used to raise their houses — ringed by a flower garland.
MP.hook: Just off these islands is the Mariana Trench, the deepest point in any ocean at nearly 11 km. Fewer people have been to the bottom of it than have walked on the Moon.

MQ.flag: Flies the French tricolour; a blue and white flag with four snakes was dropped in 2018 over its slavery-era associations.
MQ.hook: In 1902 Mount Pelée destroyed the city of Saint-Pierre in minutes and killed about 30,000 people. Two or three survived, one of them a prisoner in a thick-walled cell.

MR.flag: Green with a gold crescent and star, bordered top and bottom by red bands added in 2017 for the blood of those who resisted colonisation.
MR.hook: The last country on Earth to abolish slavery, in 1981, and it did not make it a crime until 2007. From orbit its most striking feature is the Richat Structure, a 40 km bullseye in the desert.

MS.flag: A blue ensign with a woman in green holding a harp and a cross — Erin, the personification of Ireland.
MS.hook: The Emerald Isle of the Caribbean, settled by Irish indentured workers, and the only place outside Ireland where St Patrick's Day is a public holiday. Its capital was buried by a volcano in 1997 and abandoned.

MT.flag: White and red, with the George Cross in the corner — a British medal for bravery awarded in 1942 to the entire island, which was bombed more heavily than anywhere else in the war.
MT.hook: It is the only country that flies a foreign country's medal on its flag. Malta is also the smallest EU state and speaks the only Semitic language written in the Latin alphabet.

MU.flag: Four equal horizontal bands — red, blue, yellow, green — which almost no other flag does.
MU.hook: The dodo lived only here and was gone within about a century of humans arriving. It is now on the national coat of arms, holding up the shield.

MV.flag: A red border around a green field with a white crescent. Red for blood, green for palms, the crescent for Islam.
MV.hook: The lowest country on Earth, averaging about 1.5 m above the sea. Its government once held a cabinet meeting underwater in scuba gear to make the point.

MW.flag: Black, red and green with a rising red sun on the black band — the dawn of African independence.
MW.hook: Lake Malawi holds more fish species than any other lake on the planet, most of them found nowhere else, and takes up a fifth of the country.

MX.flag: Green, white and red around an eagle perched on a prickly pear cactus, eating a snake.
MX.hook: That is the omen the Mexica were told to look for when choosing where to build their city. They found it on an island in a lake, and built Tenochtitlán there. Mexico City stands on the drained lake and is sinking into it, in places by 50 cm a year.

MY.flag: Fourteen red and white stripes and a crescent with a fourteen-pointed star — thirteen states plus the federal territories. At a glance it reads as the American flag.
MY.hook: Malaysia is split in two by 640 km of sea, with half on the mainland and half on Borneo. Its king is elected — nine hereditary rulers take five-year turns.

MZ.flag: Green, black and yellow with a red triangle, and an emblem of a book, a hoe and an AK-47 crossed over a star.
MZ.hook: The only national flag in the world with a modern assault rifle on it. Mozambique also joined the Commonwealth without ever having been British.

NA.flag: A red diagonal edged in white, splitting blue from green, with a gold sun of twelve rays in the upper corner.
NA.hook: The first country to write environmental protection into its constitution. The Namib is the oldest desert on Earth, and its dunes run straight into the Atlantic along a shore littered with shipwrecks.

NC.flag: Officially the French tricolour, but the Kanak flag — blue, red and green with a yellow disc and a flèche faîtière — flies alongside it by law.
NC.hook: One of very few places to fly two official flags side by side as a political settlement. It holds a quarter of the world's nickel and a barrier reef second only to Australia's.

NE.flag: Orange, white and green with an orange disc in the middle for the sun over the Sahara.
NE.hook: Niger once had the loneliest tree on Earth — the Tree of Ténéré, the only one for 400 km in any direction, used as a landmark by caravans. A truck driver hit it in 1973.

NF.flag: Green, white, green with a Norfolk Island pine in the middle.
NF.hook: Settled by Bounty mutineers' descendants moved from Pitcairn in 1856. Many islanders still speak Norfuk, a blend of 18th-century English and Tahitian.

NG.flag: Green, white, green — forest, peace, forest. A 23-year-old student won the design competition in 1959; the judges removed the red sun he had drawn in the middle.
NG.hook: The most populous country in Africa, with over 500 languages. Nollywood turns out more films per year than Hollywood.

NI.flag: Blue, white, blue with a triangle containing volcanoes, a Phrygian cap and a rainbow.
NI.hook: That rainbow makes Nicaragua one of only two countries with purple in its flag. Lake Nicaragua is the only freshwater lake in the world with its own sharks, which swim up the river from the sea.

NL.flag: Red, white and blue — but the top stripe was originally orange, for William of Orange. Which is why the Dutch turn up to football in orange, not red.
NL.hook: A third of the country sits below sea level and was dredged out of the water by hand. The Dutch are also the tallest people on Earth.
NL.capital: Amsterdam is the capital, but the government, parliament and king all work in The Hague.

NO.flag: The Danish flag with a blue cross laid inside the white — Denmark's history plus the red-white-blue of liberty.
NO.hook: Cut up Norway's flag and you can make the flags of six other countries inside it, including Finland, France, Indonesia, Poland and Thailand. Norway also knighted a penguin who is now a brigadier in the Norwegian Guard.

NP.flag: The only national flag that is not a rectangle — two stacked pennants carrying a moon and a sun. Its exact proportions are set out as a geometric construction inside the constitution.
NP.hook: The sun and moon mean the nation should last as long as they do. Nepal also holds eight of the world's ten highest mountains, and its calendar runs about 57 years ahead of the Gregorian one.

NR.flag: Blue with a thin gold stripe across it and a white twelve-pointed star below — and the layout is a map. The gold line is the equator, and the star sits exactly where Nauru sits just south of it.
NR.hook: The world's smallest republic got briefly rich strip-mining a century of seabird droppings, then ran out. Four-fifths of the island is now unusable mined-out rock, and there is no capital city, just a district where the offices are.

NU.flag: Rare among Pacific flags for its yellow field, with a Union Jack carrying five stars.
NU.hook: One of the world's largest raised coral atolls and one of the least visited places on Earth, with about 1,700 residents. Niue made its whole territory a marine park and once tried to give every resident free wifi.

NZ.flag: A blue ensign with the Union Jack and the four red, white-edged stars of the Southern Cross.
NZ.hook: The quickest way to tell it from Australia's: New Zealand has four stars and they are red; Australia has six and they are white. New Zealand was also the first country to give women the vote, in 1893.

OM.flag: White, red and green with the national emblem at the hoist: a curved khanjar dagger crossed over two swords.
OM.hook: The oldest continuously independent state in the Arab world. Its mountains produced frankincense so valuable that it was traded by weight against gold.

PA.flag: Quartered into white, red, white and blue with a blue and a red star — the two stars and quarters were meant to hold the country's two rival political parties in balance.
PA.hook: Because the isthmus curves, the canal runs roughly north-south, and a ship crossing from the Pacific to the Atlantic travels east to west. In Panama City the sun rises over the Pacific.

PE.flag: Red, white, red in vertical bands. The story goes that San Martín saw a flock of flamingos take off — red wings, white bodies — and took it as an omen.
PE.hook: Peru grows over 4,000 varieties of potato, nearly every potato on Earth traces back to the Andes, and Machu Picchu was unknown to the outside world until 1911.

PF.flag: Red, white, red with a canoe on the sun and waves, its outriggers carrying five figures for the five island groups.
PF.hook: 118 islands scattered across an ocean area the size of Europe. Gauguin painted here, pearls are farmed here, and the tattoo comes from here — the Tahitian word tatau.

PG.flag: Split corner to corner: black with the Southern Cross on one side, red with a golden bird-of-paradise on the other. It was designed by a 15-year-old schoolgirl in a national competition.
PG.hook: More than 800 languages are spoken here, around an eighth of all the languages on Earth, in a country of about ten million people. Mountains that high and valleys that steep kept everyone apart.

PH.flag: A white triangle with a gold sun of eight rays and three stars, over blue and red bands.
PH.hook: The only flag in the world that officially changes meaning when you turn it over: blue on top means peace, red on top means the country is at war. It is flown that way deliberately.

PK.flag: Dark green with a white crescent and star — plus a white band at the hoist that is there specifically to represent the country's religious minorities.
PK.hook: Pakistan holds K2, the hardest of the eight-thousanders, and the highest paved border crossing in the world at 4,693 m. It also has the largest ambulance network run by one charity.

PL.flag: White above red, straight off the white eagle on a red shield. Flip it and you get Indonesia and Monaco.
PL.hook: Poland has been wiped off the map entirely and come back. It also has Europe's last primeval forest and a 700-year-old salt mine with underground chapels carved from rock salt.

PM.flag: The ship Grande Hermine over waves, with a hoist strip of Basque, Breton and Norman flags for the settlers' origins.
PM.hook: The last scrap of New France, sitting 25 km off Newfoundland. During Prohibition it became a warehouse for Canadian whisky bound illegally for the United States and got very rich.

PN.flag: A blue ensign with a shield showing an anchor and a Bible from the Bounty, and a wheelbarrow with a flowering sprig.
PN.hook: About 35 people live here, descendants of the Bounty mutineers and the Tahitians who sailed with them. It is one of the least populated jurisdictions in the world and takes days to reach by boat.

PR.flag: Cuba's flag with the red and blue swapped — the two independence movements designed them together in the 1890s.
PR.hook: Puerto Ricans are US citizens who cannot vote for president while living there. El Yunque is the only tropical rainforest in the US forest system, and the coquí frog that sings there is the island's emblem.

PS.flag: Black, white and green with a red triangle — the pan-Arab colours in the arrangement first flown in the 1916 Arab Revolt.
PS.hook: It is the same flag as Jordan's, minus the seven-pointed star. Jericho, in the West Bank, is one of the oldest continuously inhabited towns anywhere, at around 11,000 years.

PT.flag: Green and red behind an armillary sphere — a navigator's instrument — wrapped around a shield of seven castles taken from the Moors and five small shields for five defeated kings.
PT.hook: Portugal has the oldest fixed borders in Europe, essentially unchanged since 1297. It also supplies half the world's cork, and its language is spoken by more people in Brazil than anywhere else.

PW.flag: A gold disc on light blue — and it is the moon, not the sun. It sits slightly toward the hoist so it looks centred when the flag flies.
PW.hook: Palau reckons the full moon is the best time to fish, plant and harvest, so the moon got the flag. It was also the first country to ban reef-damaging sunscreen, and has a lake full of jellyfish that lost their sting.

PY.flag: Red, white and blue — and the emblem in the middle is different on each side. The front has the national star; turn it over and you get the treasury seal with a lion.
PY.hook: It is the only national flag in the world with different designs on its two faces. Paraguay is also one of only two landlocked countries in the Americas, and it runs on a navy anyway.

QA.flag: Maroon and white with nine points along the join. It started out red, but the natural dye baked to maroon in the Gulf sun and Qatar kept the accident.
QA.hook: It is the only national flag more than twice as wide as it is tall. Qatar also has the highest ratio of foreign-born residents anywhere — most of the people in the country are not citizens.

RE.flag: Flies the French tricolour; unofficial local designs show a volcano and rays.
RE.hook: A French island east of Madagascar holding one of the most active volcanoes on Earth, which erupts most years. It also holds the world record for the most rain in 24 hours: 1.825 m.

RO.flag: Blue, yellow, red in vertical bands — and all but identical to Chad's. The two countries have argued about it at the UN.
RO.hook: Romanian is a Latin language marooned among Slavic ones. The country also holds the world's heaviest building, Ceaușescu's parliament palace, which weighs over four million tonnes.

RS.flag: Russia's flag upside down, with a double-headed eagle and a shield holding four Cyrillic С's — firesteels, for 'only unity saves the Serbs'.
RS.hook: Serbia gave the world the word 'vampire' and the physicist Nikola Tesla, whose ashes sit in a gold sphere in Belgrade.

RU.flag: White, blue, red — Peter the Great went to the Netherlands to learn shipbuilding, liked the Dutch flag, and rearranged it.
RU.hook: Russia spans eleven time zones and touches fourteen countries. It has so much surface area that it is closer to Alaska than Alaska is to the rest of the United States.

RW.flag: Blue, yellow and green with a gold sun in the corner. It was designed in 2001 specifically to replace a flag that had become tied to the genocide.
RW.hook: Rwanda banned plastic bags in 2008 and searches luggage for them at the airport. On the last Saturday of every month the whole country stops for a morning of compulsory community work.

SA.flag: Green with the Islamic declaration of faith above a sword. Because the text is sacred, the flag is never lowered to half-mast, and it is printed in mirror image on the reverse so the words read correctly from both sides.
SA.hook: There are no permanent rivers anywhere in the country. Saudi Arabia is also one of the few nations named after the family that runs it.

SB.flag: Blue and green divided by a thin yellow diagonal, with five white stars in the upper corner.
SB.hook: A striking share of Solomon Islanders have naturally blond hair with very dark skin — the result of a gene found almost nowhere else, and nothing to do with European ancestry. Guadalcanal, one of the islands, was the turning point of the Pacific war.

SC.flag: Five bands of blue, yellow, red, white and green fanning out from the bottom corner — no other national flag radiates like this.
SC.hook: The rays mean a young country moving into the future. Seychelles also grows the coco de mer, which produces the largest and heaviest seed of any plant in the world.

SD.flag: Red, white and black with a green triangle at the hoist.
SD.hook: Sudan has roughly twice as many pyramids as Egypt — around 200 of them at Meroë — and almost nobody visits. They are steeper and smaller, built by the Kushite kings who once ruled Egypt.

SE.flag: A gold Nordic cross on blue, from the three gold crowns on a blue shield that have stood for Sweden since the 1300s.
SE.hook: Sweden has not fought a war since 1814. It imports rubbish from other countries because its waste-to-energy plants run short, and it has roughly 270,000 islands.

SG.flag: Red over white with a crescent and five stars. The crescent is a young country on the rise; the stars are democracy, peace, progress, justice and equality.
SG.hook: One of only three true city-states left. It is physically growing — a quarter of its land has been reclaimed from the sea — and it really does fine you for selling chewing gum.

SH.flag: A blue ensign with a shield showing a ship and the wirebird, a plover found nowhere else.
SH.hook: Napoleon died in exile here, on an island so remote it is 1,900 km from Africa. It had no airport at all until 2016, and the first one built was briefly unusable because of dangerous wind shear.

SI.flag: White, blue, red with a shield of Mount Triglav, two wavy lines for the sea and rivers, and three stars from a medieval county.
SI.hook: Triglav is on the flag because every Slovene is supposed to climb it once in their life. Over half the country is forest, and it has more than 10,000 karst caves.

SJ.hook: Svalbard holds the Global Seed Vault, a bunker in permafrost storing over a million crop seed samples. A treaty lets citizens of more than 40 countries live and work here without a visa, and polar bears outnumber people.

SK.flag: White, blue, red with a shield showing a double cross standing on three blue hills — the Tatra, Matra and Fatra mountains.
SK.hook: Slovakia has more castles per person than any country on Earth, and Bratislava is the only capital that borders two other countries.

SL.flag: Green, white and blue — the land, justice, and the harbour.
SL.hook: That blue band is specifically for Freetown's harbour, one of the largest natural deep-water harbours in the world. The city was founded as a home for freed slaves.

SM.flag: White and blue with three towers on three peaks of Monte Titano, each topped with an ostrich feather, under a crown.
SM.hook: The world's oldest surviving republic, founded in 301 AD by a stonemason hiding from Roman persecution. In WWII this country of 15,000 sheltered more than 100,000 refugees.

SN.flag: Green, yellow and red vertical bands with a green five-pointed star in the middle.
SN.hook: Lake Retba turns bubblegum pink from salt-loving algae, and Senegal's westernmost point is the furthest west the African mainland goes.

SO.flag: A single white five-pointed star on light blue. The blue was a nod to the UN, which administered the territory before independence.
SO.hook: The star's five points are the five regions where ethnic Somalis live, only two of which are inside the country. Somalia has the longest mainland coastline in Africa.

SR.flag: Green, white and red with a large gold star in the centre.
SR.hook: The most forested country on Earth, at over 90% tree cover. It is also one of the most ethnically mixed places anywhere — Dutch is official, but Hindi, Javanese, Chinese and a creole are all spoken daily.

SS.flag: Black, red and green separated by white, with a blue triangle and a gold star.
SS.hook: The youngest country in the world, independent since July 2011. The Sudd, its vast swamp, is so impenetrable that it stopped Roman expeditions from finding the source of the Nile.

ST.flag: Green, yellow and green with a red triangle and two black stars — one star per island.
ST.hook: The equator runs right through one of its islets, so you can stand with a foot in each hemisphere. For a while it produced more cocoa per hectare than anywhere on Earth.

SV.flag: Blue, white, blue with the coat of arms — the blue bands are the Pacific and the Caribbean, even though El Salvador only touches one of them.
SV.hook: The smallest country in Central America and the only one with no Caribbean coast. It has around twenty volcanoes and is nicknamed the land of them.

SX.flag: The Dutch red, white and blue rearranged into a triangle and two bands, with the island's arms.
SX.hook: The Dutch half of the island shared with French Saint Martin. Its airport is famous for jets passing a few metres over the heads of people on Maho Beach.

SY.flag: Green, white and black with three red stars — the 1932 independence flag, brought back in 2024.
SY.hook: Damascus has been continuously inhabited for perhaps 11,000 years, which makes it a serious contender for the oldest city still standing.

SZ.flag: Blue, yellow and red with a black and white Nguni ox-hide shield laid on two spears and a staff, all shown horizontally.
SZ.hook: It changed its name from Swaziland in 2018 partly because people abroad kept confusing it with Switzerland. It is one of the last absolute monarchies on Earth.
SZ.capital: Lobamba is the royal and legislative capital; Mbabane handles administration.

TC.flag: A blue ensign with a shield holding a conch shell, a spiny lobster and a turk's cap cactus.
TC.hook: The cactus on the shield is what the islands are named after — its red top looks like a Turkish fez. Early printings of the flag mistook the conch shell for a door and added a handle.

TD.flag: Blue, yellow, red — and all but indistinguishable from Romania's, which Chad has formally complained about at the UN.
TD.hook: Lake Chad has lost about 90% of its surface since the 1960s. The country also holds the Sahara's largest mountain range and a fossil skull that pushed human ancestry back seven million years.

TF.flag: The French tricolour in the canton on a blue field, with a lyre-shaped emblem and three stars.
TF.hook: France's sub-Antarctic islands have no permanent population, just rotating scientists — and a few million penguins, which comfortably outnumber every human who has ever set foot there.

TG.flag: Five green and yellow stripes with a red square and a white star in the corner — five stripes for five regions.
TG.hook: Togo is a long thin strip barely 56 km wide where it meets the sea, running 550 km inland. That shape is a straight leftover of colonial map-drawing.

TH.flag: Red, white, blue, white, red. The blue centre stripe was added during WWI to align with the Allies — and it happens to be the king's colour.
TH.hook: The only country in Southeast Asia never colonised by a European power. Its capital's full ceremonial name runs to 168 letters and is the longest place name in the world.
TH.capital: Bangkok is the short version. Thais call it Krung Thep, 'city of angels'.

TJ.flag: Red, white and green with a gold crown under seven stars — seven being the perfect number in Tajik tradition.
TJ.hook: 93% of the country is mountain. It also briefly held the world's tallest flagpole at 165 m, an arms race it lost to Saudi Arabia.

TK.flag: Yellow with a Tokelauan canoe sailing toward the Southern Cross.
TK.hook: Three atolls with about 1,500 people, no airport, and the only way in is a boat from Samoa. Tokelau runs almost entirely on solar power, and its .tk domain was for years given away free, briefly making it the most-registered domain on Earth.

TL.flag: Red with a black triangle over a yellow one and a white star — yellow for colonialism, black for the obscurantism to be overcome, white for peace.
TL.hook: One of the youngest countries on Earth, independent only since 2002. It uses the US dollar but mints its own coins, and Portuguese is still an official language.

TM.flag: The most intricate national flag in the world. A green field with a crescent and five stars, and a vertical stripe of carpet design showing five gül — the medallions of the five tribes — above an olive branch.
TM.hook: A gas crater in the Karakum desert has been burning continuously since 1971, when geologists set it alight expecting it to go out in weeks. Locals call it the Door to Hell.

TN.flag: Red with a white disc holding a red crescent and star. Its design predates independence by a century, going back to the Ottoman navy.
TN.hook: Carthage was here, and Rome ploughed it under. Much of Star Wars was shot in the south — the planet Tatooine takes its name from the real town of Tataouine.

TO.flag: Red with a white canton holding a red cross. The original design was an all-white flag with a red cross, until Tonga noticed that was already the Red Cross.
TO.hook: The only Pacific island nation never colonised. Its constitution states that the flag can never be changed.

TR.flag: A white crescent and star on red. The legend says a commander saw them reflected in a pool of his soldiers' blood after battle.
TR.hook: Istanbul is the only city sitting on two continents. Türkiye also grows around 70% of the world's hazelnuts, so most chocolate spread on Earth starts here.

TT.flag: Red with a black diagonal edged in white, running from the upper hoist to the lower fly.
TT.hook: The steelpan was invented here in the 1930s out of discarded oil drums, and is generally called the only acoustic instrument invented in the 20th century. The island also has a 40-hectare lake of natural asphalt.

TV.flag: Light blue with the Union Jack and nine yellow stars — and the stars are a map, laid out in the real geographic positions of the nine islands.
TV.hook: Tuvalu makes a large share of its national income renting out its internet domain, .tv, to television companies. It is also one of the lowest-lying countries on Earth and is building a digital copy of itself in case the sea takes the original.

TW.flag: Red with a blue canton holding a white sun of twelve rays — the twelve two-hour periods of the traditional Chinese day.
TW.hook: Produces the overwhelming majority of the world's most advanced computer chips. Two-thirds of the island is steep forested mountain, with more than 250 peaks above 3,000 m.

TZ.flag: Green and blue split by a black diagonal edged in gold — land, sea, people and mineral wealth.
TZ.hook: The name is a portmanteau: Tanganyika plus Zanzibar, merged in 1964. Kilimanjaro is the tallest free-standing mountain on Earth, rising straight off the plain with no range behind it.
TZ.capital: Dodoma is the official capital, but most government business still happens in Dar es Salaam.

UA.flag: The simplest landscape painting in the world: blue sky over a yellow wheat field.
UA.hook: Ukraine sits on a quarter of the planet's black soil, the richest farmland there is. It also holds the deepest metro station on Earth, 105 m under Kyiv.

UG.flag: Six stripes of black, yellow and red repeated, with a grey crowned crane in a white disc.
UG.hook: The crane is shown standing on one leg, which is meant to say the country is always moving forward. Uganda holds the source of the Nile and more than half the world's remaining mountain gorillas.

UM.flag: Flies the flag of the United States.
UM.hook: Nine scattered islands and atolls with no permanent residents, including Wake, Midway and Baker. Most are wildlife refuges; one, Navassa, is also claimed by Haiti.

US.flag: Thirteen stripes for the original colonies, fifty stars for the states. It has been formally redesigned 27 times as states joined.
US.hook: The current 50-star arrangement was drawn by a 17-year-old for a school project in 1958. His teacher gave him a B−, then raised it to an A when Congress adopted the design.

UY.flag: Nine white and blue stripes with a Sun of May in the corner — the same faced sun as Argentina's, from the same revolution.
UY.hook: Nine stripes for the nine original departments. Uruguay hosted and won the first football World Cup in 1930, and was the first country in the world to legalise cannabis nationally.

UZ.flag: Blue, white and green separated by thin red lines, with a crescent and twelve stars for the months of the year.
UZ.hook: One of only two doubly landlocked countries on Earth — you must cross two international borders to reach any ocean. The other is Liechtenstein.

VA.flag: Square, gold and white, with the crossed keys of St Peter — one gold, one silver — under the papal tiara. The keys are the power to bind and loose.
VA.hook: 0.49 km², smaller than many farms, with about 800 residents and its own ATM that works in Latin. Because tourists are pickpocketed there constantly and the population is tiny, it posts the highest crime rate per capita in the world.

VC.flag: Blue, gold and green with three green diamonds arranged in a V — for Vincent, and for the Gems of the Antilles.
VC.hook: The diamonds are literally arranged into the country's initial. Its volcano, La Soufrière, has erupted five times in the last 300 years, most recently in 2021.

VE.flag: Yellow, blue and red with an arc of eight white stars, and a coat of arms with a galloping white horse.
VE.hook: There were seven stars for 150 years until 2006, when an eighth was added to honour a wish Simón Bolívar had expressed in 1817. Venezuela also has Angel Falls, which drops 979 m — so far that much of the water becomes mist before it lands.

VG.flag: A blue ensign with the arms of Saint Ursula: a woman holding a lamp, surrounded by eleven more.
VG.hook: Columbus named the islands for Saint Ursula and her legendary 11,000 virgin companions. The territory uses the US dollar despite being British.

VI.flag: White with a yellow eagle holding an olive branch and three arrows, between the letters V and I.
VI.hook: The United States bought these islands from Denmark in 1917 for $25 million in gold, worried Germany might take them and threaten the Panama Canal. They are the only part of the US where people drive on the left.

VN.flag: A single large gold star on red, one point per class: workers, peasants, soldiers, intellectuals and traders.
VN.hook: Vietnam grows most of the world's robusta coffee, and Hang Son Doong is so vast it holds its own jungle, river and weather, with clouds forming inside the cave.

VU.flag: Red and green split by a black triangle and a gold Y, with a boar's tusk curled around two crossed namele fern leaves.
VU.hook: The Y follows the shape of the archipelago. A curled boar's tusk means prosperity, and the ferns mean peace. Vanuatu has more languages per person than any country on Earth, and land divers here jump from wooden towers with vines tied to their ankles — the practice bungee jumping was copied from.

WF.flag: Red with a white Maltese-style cross in a blue canton carrying the French tricolour.
WF.hook: A French collectivity in the Pacific with three traditional kings still recognised alongside the French administration. Wallis and Futuna are 230 km apart and speak different languages.

WS.flag: Red with a blue canton holding the Southern Cross — five stars rather than the usual four.
WS.hook: At the end of 2011 Samoa skipped 30 December entirely, jumping west across the date line to stop being 21 hours behind Australia and New Zealand, its main trading partners. Nobody born that day has a birthday.

XK.flag: Blue with the country's own outline in gold and six white stars — one of only two flags that map themselves, along with Cyprus.
XK.hook: Declared independence in 2008 and is recognised by about half the world's countries. Like Bosnia's, the flag was designed to avoid any colour associated with a particular ethnic group.

YE.flag: Red, white, black and nothing else — the plainest of all the pan-Arab tricolours.
YE.hook: Socotra island, off the coast, is so isolated that a third of its plants grow nowhere else, including umbrella-shaped dragon's blood trees that bleed red sap. Mainland Shibam is a 16th-century city of mudbrick tower blocks nicknamed the Manhattan of the desert.

YT.flag: Flies the French tricolour, alongside a local flag with two seahorses and a crescent.
YT.hook: In 1974 Mayotte voted to stay French while the rest of the Comoros chose independence, so it is now an EU outermost region in the Mozambique Channel — and Comoros still claims it.

ZA.flag: Six colours in a horizontal Y — more than any other national flag, and it carries no emblem at all.
ZA.hook: The Y is convergence: separate roads joining into one. The country also has three capitals and twelve official languages, and its anthem switches between five of them.

ZM.flag: Green with an orange eagle above three vertical bars of red, black and orange — and the whole emblem is pushed into the bottom right corner, which almost no flag does.
ZM.hook: The off-centre design is deliberate. Zambia shares Victoria Falls with Zimbabwe, where a natural rock pool at the lip lets people swim to the edge of a 100 m drop.

ZW.flag: Seven stripes with a white triangle holding a red star and the Zimbabwe Bird — a soapstone carving found in the ruins of Great Zimbabwe.
ZW.hook: Great Zimbabwe was a stone city of 18,000 people built without mortar, and colonial authorities spent decades insisting Africans could not have built it. The country later printed a 100 trillion dollar note.
